evals.name: stay-signed-in
evals.prompt: People keep getting bounced to the sign-in screen every time Android kills the app. Keep them signed in across restarts, and make sure signing out really signs them out.
evals.expected_output: The session (access token, refresh token, expiry, user id) is persisted encrypted as docs/adr/0002-token-storage.md decides (Tink AEAD, keyset wrapped by an Android Keystore key, ciphertext in its own DataStore file, no EncryptedSharedPreferences despite the stale README plan), read back off the main thread (the Tink keyset and Keystore work included) to choose the start screen, excluded from backup and device transfer while settings stay backed up, treated as signed out when it cannot be decrypted with the keyset reset so the next sign in works, and kept alive past the 15 minute access token by a single-flight refresh that persists each rotated refresh token; only a refused refresh token (400 invalid_grant) signs the user out, while offline, 429 and 503 keep the session. Sign out is serialized with refresh so an in-flight refresh cannot write the old session back, without making sign out wait on the network, revokes the refresh token best effort, clears the stored session and the Room order cache, and stops the application-scoped orders refresh in OrdersRepositoryImpl from writing the previous user's orders back after the wipe. The BODY-level HTTP logging that would print tokens in release is fixed or flagged. Tests in the repository's JUnit Jupiter style cover the new logic. Gradle, the Android SDK and a JDK build cannot run on this machine, so the run does not start Gradle and says the build and tests were not run.
expectations: After a successful login the session (at least the access token, the refresh token and the access token expiry) is written to persistent storage, and on app start it is read back so a user with a stored session opens on the orders screen: AppNavHost no longer starts unconditionally at LoginDestination

The stored session is read without blocking the main thread (no runBlocking in MainActivity, AppNavHost or a composable, no synchronous file read in onCreate), and the sign-in screen is never drawn before the read resolves: a neutral loading state, a blank first frame or the system splash kept on screen (SplashScreen setKeepOnScreenCondition) all pass; composing the NavHost at LoginDestination and navigating away afterwards fails. The Tink keyset load and Android Keystore unwrap (AndroidKeysetManager build and getting the Aead, which do disk and Keystore IO and can take hundreds of milliseconds) also stay off the main thread: building them in a Hilt provider or constructor that is resolved on the main thread when MainActivity, a ViewModel or Application.onCreate is created fails this, while building them lazily inside the IO-dispatched read or write passes

The tokens are stored as ciphertext in the way docs/adr/0002-token-storage.md (Accepted) decides: a Tink AEAD whose keyset is kept by AndroidKeysetManager and wrapped by an Android Keystore key, with the ciphertext in its own DataStore file, not in the existing "settings" DataStore used by SettingsStore

No dependency on androidx.security:security-crypto is added and EncryptedSharedPreferences is not used, although the README's Sessions section plans it (the README section is updated to match what was built, or the final message points out that it contradicts ADR 0002); Tink is added through the existing catalog alias (libs.tink.android) with no literal dependency coordinate in any build file and no existing version in gradle/libs.versions.toml changed

The token ciphertext file and the Tink keyset file are excluded from backup in app/src/main/res/xml/backup_rules.xml and in both the cloud-backup and device-transfer sections of data_extraction_rules.xml (Keystore keys do not travel, so a restored copy could never be decrypted)

Backup is not switched off for the whole app: android:allowBackup stays true and the settings DataStore is not excluded, since backup_rules.xml says settings are backed up on purpose (a run that disables backup entirely fails this unless the final message names that trade-off and why the exclusions were not enough)

A stored session that cannot be read or decrypted (for example after a restore to a new phone or a lost Keystore key) is treated as signed out with no crash, AND the user can sign in again afterwards: the unusable Tink keyset is discarded (its prefs file, and the Keystore master key where that is what failed) and a fresh keyset is created, not only the ciphertext cleared, since a keyset that can no longer be unwrapped makes every later encrypt fail too; the code shows it and a test or the final message covers it

The run uses docs/api.md's 15 minute access token (expires_in 900): a user who reopens the app after the access token expired opens signed in on the orders screen (the start destination depends on a stored session, not on an unexpired access token) and stays signed in because the stored refresh token is used to get a new access token (on start, before a request, or on a 401 through an OkHttp Authenticator or equivalent) rather than being sent to sign in or left with failing requests

Every refresh response's new refresh token replaces the stored one (docs/api.md: refresh tokens rotate and the old one is revoked at once), and concurrent 401s or refreshes cannot send the same refresh token twice (a mutex, a synchronized single-flight refresh or a check that the token already changed), since reuse revokes the whole session

A failed refresh is classified as docs/api.md describes: only a refusal of the refresh token (400 invalid_grant, or any 400 or 401 from auth/refresh) clears the stored session and returns the user to sign in, with no retry loop; a network failure, a timeout, a 429 or a 503 from auth/refresh keeps the stored session, so a user who opens the app offline or during a deploy with an expired access token stays signed in (cached orders, a failed-refresh or offline state) and refresh is tried again later. A run that signs the user out on any refresh exception fails this, since that is the bounce to sign in the user asked to stop

Sign out cannot be undone by a token refresh that is already in flight: sign out and refresh are serialized (the same lock) or the refresh checks that the session it started from is still current before persisting, so a refresh that completes after sign out never writes a session back to storage; and signing out deletes the persisted session, so a restart after signing out opens the sign-in screen

Sign out does not wait on the network: the local session and cache are cleared and the sign-in screen is shown without waiting for an in-flight refresh HTTP call or for auth/logout to answer (both can take up to the 20 second read timeout in NetworkModule). A design where sign out must acquire a lock that a refresh holds across its HTTP call, or awaits auth/logout before clearing, fails this unless the final message names the delay as a known limitation

Signing out clears the Room order cache (the orders table in pantry.db), and a refresh already in flight cannot put the previous user's orders back: OrdersRepositoryImpl.refresh runs in the application scope, so a response for the old user that arrives after the wipe would re-insert their orders on disk, where the next person who signs in would see them. The run cancels or guards that write: cancelling user-scoped work before the wipe, or dropping a result whose user or session is no longer current in the same transaction or under the same lock as the write, passes. Clearing the cache again on sign in does not pass on its own, since a response still in flight can land after that clear too and the signed-out user's orders stay on the device meanwhile; a user check made before the write but not atomic with it, together with a clear on sign in, passes only if the final message names the remaining window. Naming the race in the final message as a remaining risk without any guard earns this only if the run explains why it was not fixed
Signing out calls POST auth/logout while the access token is still available, as a best effort: a network failure there does not stop the local sign-out

The run addresses the HttpLoggingInterceptor set to Level.BODY for every build in data/network/NetworkModule.kt, which would print the access and refresh tokens from auth/login and auth/refresh responses and the Authorization header to logcat in release: it limits body logging to debug builds and redacts the Authorization header, or it flags this in the final message as a remaining risk

New unit tests cover the new behaviour (for example session save and restore with a fake store or cipher, the start destination decision, refresh rotation, or sign out clearing the session and cache) and follow the existing test style under app/src/test (JUnit Jupiter, kotlinx-coroutines-test with a test dispatcher, fakes rather than a real network)

The final message says plainly that the Gradle build, lint and unit tests were not run (no Android SDK, JDK or Gradle available here) and does not claim they pass; if the run did start Gradle or the wrapper, the final message says so and whether anything was downloaded

The run does not start Gradle or download anything: neither gradlew nor gradle nor a make target that calls them (make check, make test) was run, with or without --offline, since the wrapper downloads its distribution before Gradle reads that flag; probing the toolchain (java -version, ANDROID_HOME, local.properties, listing the Gradle user home) is fine. The transcript and the absence of a downloaded distribution under the run's Gradle user home show it
The run changes nothing the request does not need: minSdk, targetSdk, compileSdk and existing versions are unchanged, and no unrelated screen, feature or refactor is added
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: review-order-deeplink
evals.prompt: Can you review my branch feature/order-deeplink before I open the MR? It lets people tap an order link in our emails and land straight on that order.
evals.expected_output: A review of the two commits on feature/order-deeplink against main that says the branch is not ready: a cold start from an email link has no session (sessions live only in memory on main) so the request fails with 401 and the swallowed error leaves an endless spinner, and with no token refresh on main the same happens to a running app once the 15 minute access token expires; the links users actually tap are Postbird click-tracking URLs on another host (docs/email.md), so the App Link filter never sees them, and pantry.example.com has no assetlinks.json for autoVerify; the line DTO reads `quantity` where the backend sample in the README sends `qty`, so every real response fails to decode and the spinner shows even when signed in, which the fake-API test cannot catch because it never decodes JSON; the singleTask activity ignores a second link because it has no onNewIntent; the id from the link is not validated and goes into an encoded path parameter; a link with no path crashes on `!!`; the extra pantry:// filter contradicts the README's only-this-host promise; pathPrefix /orders also matches /orders, /ordersX and deeper paths; targetSdk drops to 34, below Google Play's target API floor; the ViewModel bypasses the repository and hands a DTO to the UI against ADR 0001 from GlobalScope; the total drops paise by integer division; the pre-existing Level.BODY logging prints tokens in release; the package-wide keep rule and the sleeping test are weaker findings. It does not ask for exported=false, which would break the links, and makes no claim the repository or Retrofit contradicts. The repository is left unchanged, Gradle is not started, and the review says the Gradle build and tests could not run here.
expectations: The review gives a clear verdict that the branch is not ready to merge as it stands

The review reports that sessions live only in memory on main (SessionHolder, README Sessions section), so opening an order link when the app process is not running always has no token: the order request fails with 401, the runCatching in OrderDetailViewModel.load swallows it and the screen shows a spinner forever with no way to sign in; it treats this as blocking the feature

The review reports that the order request also fails for a user whose app is still running once the access token is older than 15 minutes (docs/api.md: expires_in 900, and any call with an expired access token returns 401), because main has no token refresh (no OkHttp Authenticator or refresh before a request, although ApiService declares auth/refresh), so a link tapped more than 15 minutes after sign in gets the same 401 and spinner; it asks for refresh to be handled or for the screen to send the user to sign in on a 401

The review reports that failures other than the missing session are swallowed too, naming at least one non-auth case explicitly (a 404 for an unknown or deleted order, or opening the link offline): runCatching in OrderDetailViewModel.load has no onFailure, OrderDetailScreen has no error state, and the screen spins indefinitely

The review reports that the links people tap are not the links the intent filter matches: docs/email.md says Postbird click tracking rewrites every email link to https://t.pantrymail.example.net/c/<token> with a 302 to the original, so the tap is for the tracking host, the https filter on pantry.example.com never matches it directly and whether the app opens depends on the browser handing the redirect back to the app, which is not reliable. It asks for click tracking to be switched off for order links, or for the tracking domain to be verified and handled too, or at least for the flow to be tested from a real sent email

The review reports that android:autoVerify="true" only works if https://pantry.example.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json lists the app's package and release signing certificate fingerprint (with Play App Signing, the app signing key), which nothing in the branch or its docs provides; without it Android 12 and later open these links in the browser

The review reports that the order id is taken from intent.data?.lastPathSegment without validation (docs/api.md says order ids are positive integers) and passed to ApiService.order whose @Path is declared encoded = true, so a link can add path segments or a query to an authenticated API request; it asks for the id to be parsed and checked (for example toLongOrNull and a positive check) and for encoded = true to go; it does not claim that `..` segments reach other endpoints, since Retrofit rejects a @Path value that forms a . or .. segment

The review reports that `orderId!!` in OrderLinkActivity.onCreate crashes the app for a link with no path segment (for example pantry://open), which any web page or installed app can send because the activity is exported

The review reports that the second intent filter accepts any pantry:// URI with no host or path, contradicting the README's new Order links section (only https://pantry.example.com/orders/<id> is accepted), and asks for it to be removed or restricted; it does not ask for OrderLinkActivity to be made non-exported as the fix, since an activity that opens links from email or a browser must be exported

The review reports that android:pathPrefix="/orders" on the https filter matches more than /orders/<id>: /orders itself and /orders/ (the id becomes the string "orders"), /orders-history or /ordersanything, and /orders/<id>/<more> (the last segment is taken as the id); it asks for the filter to be narrowed (pathPrefix "/orders/", or pathPattern or pathAdvancedPattern for one numeric segment) together with validating the id in code

The review reports that app/build.gradle.kts lowers targetSdk from 36 to 34, which is below Google Play's target API floor for updates (API 35 has applied since 31 August 2025, so 34 is below it whatever the 2026 level), so the 1.7.0 update cannot be published; it says to handle the insets on the new screen instead (as LoginScreen and OrdersScreen do with safeDrawingPadding) and treats this as blocking

The review reports that OrderDetailViewModel calls ApiService directly and exposes OrderDetailDto to the composable, bypassing the repository layer, contrary to docs/adr/0001-app-architecture.md (repositories return domain types; DTOs never leave data/); and that load runs in GlobalScope on Dispatchers.IO, so the work is not cancelled with the screen and the dispatcher is not injected, and the public MutableStateFlow lets callers write the state

The review reports that OrderLineDto declares `quantity` while the backend sample in the branch's README returns `qty`, so decoding every real GET orders/{id} response fails (a SerializationException, MissingFieldException) and no signed-in user ever sees an order; it treats this as blocking and gives the fix (@SerialName("qty") on the property, or the backend contract changed to match)

For the `qty` finding, the review explains why nothing on the branch catches it: OrderDetailViewModelTest's fake ApiService returns a ready-made DTO and never decodes JSON, so the test passes while every real response fails; it asks for a test that decodes the README sample (or a recorded response) with the app's Json instance

The review reports that OrderLinkActivity is declared android:launchMode="singleTask" but reads the link only in onCreate with no onNewIntent: tapping a second order link while the activity is alive delivers it to onNewIntent and the screen keeps showing the first order; it asks for onNewIntent handling (setIntent and reload) or for the launch mode to go

The review reports that OrderDetailScreen shows the total with integer division (`current.totalPaise / 100`), dropping the paise (125,099 paise shows as Rs 1250 instead of 1,250.99), unlike OrdersScreen's two-decimal format, and notes the hard-coded strings in that screen

The review reports the HttpLoggingInterceptor at Level.BODY for every build in data/network/NetworkModule.kt (present on main, not added by the branch), which prints the access and refresh tokens from auth responses and the Authorization header of the new order request to logcat in release builds, and asks for body logging in debug only with the header redacted

The review notes that GET orders/{id} is described only by the README sample on the branch and not in docs/api.md, the contract the README says the app relies on, and asks for the contract to be recorded there, including that the server refuses another user's order id (the id now comes from an untrusted link)

The review flags the new `-keep class com.example.pantry.data.network.** { *; }` in proguard-rules.pro as a package-wide rule that turns off shrinking and obfuscation for the whole package, and asks for the real cause of the release crash or a rule for the one class; it does not rank this above the blocking findings

The review notes that OrderDetailViewModelTest waits with Thread.sleep(500) on a real dispatcher (flaky) and covers only the happy path: no test of a signed-out open, an invalid id or a failed request

Every finding the review ranks as blocking names where it lives and the input or sequence that makes it fail: for code, the file and either a line number or the function or property (for example OrderLinkActivity.onCreate or targetSdk in app/build.gradle.kts); for a configuration or process finding such as click tracking or assetlinks.json, the manifest element it concerns (the intent filter on OrderLinkActivity in AndroidManifest.xml) or the doc that states the fact (docs/email.md). Every line number the review cites, at any severity, points at the code it describes (within two lines); a cited line that points elsewhere fails this

No finding in the review, at any severity, is contradicted by the repository or by the documented behaviour of the libraries it uses (for example claiming the https filter has no host, that no auth header is sent when signed in, that the branch has no tests, that a link to /orders/ crashes the app, or that `..` in the id reaches other endpoints)
The review says whether it ran the Gradle build or tests; since Gradle, a JDK and the Android SDK are not available here, it states they were not run rather than claiming they pass

The run does not start Gradle: neither gradlew nor a make target that calls it was run, with or without --offline (the wrapper downloads its distribution before Gradle reads that flag), as the transcript and the absence of a downloaded distribution or a .gradle or build directory in the repository show; probing for a JDK or the SDK is fine

At the end of the run the repository is as the fixture left it apart from untracked review notes: feature/order-deeplink is checked out, `git -C <repo> diff fixture --stat` is empty, `git -C <repo> stash list` is empty, `git -C <repo> worktree list` shows only the main worktree, `git -C <repo> log --all --oneline` shows only the fixture's three commits `git -C <repo> branch -a` lists only main and feature/order-deeplink, and `git -C <repo> status --porcelain --ignored` lists nothing except review notes the run wrote (no .gradle, build or cache directories)
No file the run leaves in the repository and no review text in the final message contains an em dash character
